package_info.why_malicious: The package 'web-browserify' impersonates the legitimate 'browserify' library but contains a malicious postinstall script that extracts and executes a persistent ELF binary. This binary performs extensive system reconnaissance, exfiltrates sensitive information to an attacker-controlled domain, seeks elevated privileges, and attempts destructive actions such as wiping /etc/ and disabling system services. The package leverages legitimate open-source modules to evade detection and currently has a zero detection rate on VirusTotal.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Executes a Node.js script, then runs a native ELF binary extracted from an archive, and deletes the bin directory to remove evidence of the malicious binary.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The postinstall script executes a native binary and then deletes its own installation files, which is highly atypical for legitimate npm packages and is a strong indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages may use postinstall scripts for setup, but do not execute native binaries or remove their own files immediately after installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages use postinstall scripts for compiling native modules or setup, but rarely execute arbitrary binaries or self-delete installation artifacts.
key_indicators: Executes a native ELF binary during npm install
Deletes the ./bin directory immediately after execution
Chained execution of Node.js and native code in postinstall

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ELF binary 'run' extracted and executed; uses 'sudo-prompt' to request root privileges
malicious_snippets.code_language: ELF binary (compiled, uses Node.js modules internally)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Extracts itself from a compressed archive, requests elevated privileges using 'sudo-prompt', copies itself to /etc/rot1 for persistence, and configures itself to run on every system boot.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The binary requests root privileges immediately after installation, persists itself in a system directory (/etc/rot1), and ensures execution on every boot, which are all strong indicators of malware attempting to maintain control over the system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages do not install persistent binaries in system directories or require root access during installation, especially not via postinstall scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System management or installer tools may request elevation, but not as part of a third-party npm package's postinstall process.
key_indicators: Requests root/admin privileges via sudo-prompt during install
Configures binary to run on every system boot

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Uses 'systeminformation' npm module to collect system/user/hardware info; exfiltrates via HTTP GET to 'ejemplo.me'
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Performs extensive system fingerprinting, collecting user, OS, Docker, Bluetooth, VM, CPU, RAM, disk, network, and USB information, then exfiltrates this data to the attacker-controlled domain 'ejemplo.me' over unencrypted HTTP.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The binary collects a wide range of sensitive system information and exfiltrates it to an external, attacker-controlled domain, which is a hallmark of reconnaissance and data theft malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not collect and transmit detailed system reconnaissance data to unknown or suspicious domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise software may collect telemetry, but not to non-standard or suspicious domains, and not with such breadth of data.
key_indicators: Reconnaissance of user, system, and hardware information
Exfiltration of data to 'ejemplo.me' over HTTP
Use of 'systeminformation' module for broad data collection

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attempts to remove /etc/ contents and disables systemctl/systemd services
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Attempts destructive actions: wipes the /etc/ directory and disables critical Unix services using systemctl/systemd commands, potentially rendering the system unbootable or unusable.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The binary attempts to delete the contents of /etc/ and disable core system services, which is highly destructive and can result in a bricked or severely compromised system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should ever attempt to delete /etc/ or disable system services as part of its operation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for deleting /etc/ or disabling systemctl/systemd from a package install or runtime context.

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package, triggering the postinstall script defined in package.json.
attack_chain.leads_to: Extraction and execution of the malicious ELF binary.

attack_chain.action: The ELF binary is extracted from bin/run.tar.xz and executed, requesting elevated privileges via sudo-prompt.
The binary copies itself to /etc/rot1 for persistence and configures itself to run on every system boot.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ongoing malicious activity on the system.

attack_chain.action: The persistent binary performs system reconnaissance and exfiltrates collected data to the attacker-controlled domain 'ejemplo.me'.
The binary attempts destructive actions: wiping /etc/ and disabling system services (conditional on certain triggers).
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential system bricking or denial of service.

behavioral_signatures: npm postinstall script executes a native ELF binary
Immediate deletion of installation artifacts (bin directory) after execution
Binary requests root privileges via sudo-prompt during install
Persistence by copying binary to /etc/rot1 and configuring for autostart on boot
Extensive system reconnaissance and exfiltration of data to external domain
Attempts to delete /etc/ or disable systemctl/systemd services
file_indicators: Presence of bin/run.tar.xz archive in npm package
Extraction and execution of ELF binary named 'run'
Immediate removal of ./bin directory after install
network_indicators: HTTP GET requests to 'ejemplo.me' containing system fingerprinting data
Unencrypted exfiltration of sensitive information to external domain
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that execute native binaries and immediately delete installation files. Flag packages that extract and run ELF binaries, especially those requesting root privileges via sudo-prompt. Detect persistence mechanisms involving copying binaries to /etc/rot1 or similar system directories and configuring for autostart. Monitor outbound HTTP requests to suspicious domains such as 'ejemplo.me', particularly those containing system reconnaissance data. Alert on any process attempting to delete /etc/ or disable systemctl/systemd services, as these are clear indicators of destructive malware.
